title: Casual 2D Mobile game development solved
author: hydrangers
selftext:
2 months ago I decided to give AI game development a shot. I hadn't done any game development in over 15 years, so I figured it would be a fun project to kill time. I ended up recreating a game that used to be on the mobile market many years ago but had been pulled and never returned, or even cloned.

I ended up building a game where you smash ragdolls, blow them up, shoot them, freeze them, and ultimately just humiliate them for personal gain. The game is called Limb from Limb and I essentially just went into this to see how far AI has come and how capable it is with mobile game development, from design spec through to launch. Surprisingly, it was able to do pretty much everything, including submitting the game to google play and the app store.

For coding, I mostly used Claude (Fable 5 for shaders/animations, and Opus 5 for everything else), Sol 5.6 Ultra for image generation for literally all of the art, Suno for the in-game music, and elevenlabs for voices and sound effects.  
  
I think it has turned out quite nice looking for a 2d game, and fun to play for a younger audience. Let me know what you think. Again, this took 2 months to build as a 1-man show. I believe 2D game development is pretty much solved, but looking to get others opinions.

comments.author: FlipperTheRipper
comments.body:
Looks great! I making a mobile game right now but the biggest issue I’ve been having is improving the UI/UX. 

On Unity, Claude seems to struggle with using the right assets or placing them appropriately , and I always end up having to fix broken UI elements. And I suck at UI/UX dev haha

Did you develop this game on Unity? And how did you go about dealing with UI/UX?

replies.author: hydrangers
replies.body:
Thanks!  
  
Yep, I used Unity for this game. I originally started with Godot and it did fine, but moved over to Unity after I found the physics solver wasn't ideal for this type of game so I ended up switching to Unity for Box2d before I realized you can change the physics engine in Godot lol.

Surprisingly using Fable 5 for the UI was not terrible. I mostly just instructed it for each asset, for example the calendar/level selector to apply a grid overtop to properly section out and align texts before coding and positioning them. Not to say that it wasn't a struggle sometimes, and you can see it with the level failed dialog at the end of the video that they don't look super natural. A lot of the time with the rough edges of the dialogs it can get positioning wrong or just overall doesn't really make them look very good. With a couple iterations on the grid prompt and some different text styling/colors, I feel like it would be able to pass a QA check though.

As far as everything else UI/UX related, I was super detailed on how I wanted the layout to be and the design to look, for example the way the game mode and level select calendar near the start of the video how it shifts from side to side and then loads the level behind the calendar.

comments.author: PsychologicalArt2537
comments.body: How did you make the assets?

replies.author: hydrangers
replies.body: Everything was generated with chatgpt images 2 (not sure if that's the right now). I used codex for all art generation. I tried using claude to instruct codex, but the quality of image generation was far less than when using codex and sol 5.6 ultra. I also found that the limitations when using codex were FAR LESS than when using chatgpt desktop app to generate images.

replies.author: RevenueChemical6910
replies.body: Did you just ask Codex regularly? Or did you use skills and MCPs for image-gen or some such?

replies.author: hydrangers
replies.body: For the most part I just had codex and claude running in their own terminals and for image generation I prompt the codex terminal, for all other tasks I used claude. No additional skills or MCPs aside from ASC and Google play MCPs for submitting the game.
